text: High completion rates are a vanity metric if they ignore who was excluded from the start. We celebrate the students who finish, but we rarely audit the barriers that stop others. If your course isn't navigable via screen readers or lacks accurate transcripts, you aren't just losing engagement—you are actively gatekeeping knowledge. True instructional design isn't just about the quality of your curriculum; it’s about ensuring the architecture of your platform allows every student to actually reach the finish line.

Topic: online course completion: identify an accessibility blind spot

Here is a rough draft of a Substack Note:
"""
We often celebrate high completion rates, but we rarely ask who is left behind along the way. If your course isn't navigable via screen readers or lacks accurate transcripts, you're inadvertently excluding a segment of your audience before they even hit module one. We need to move beyond just making great content and start auditing for inclusive design. True engagement isn't just about the curriculum; it's about ensuring every student has the tools to actually cross the finish line.
